correctness.rationale: The physical root of the centroid equation exists uniquely because F_q is positive and F has opposite signs at the interval endpoints. Pentagon support and polar identities and its centroid are explicitly verified. The exact area and covariance formulas reduce Hessian inertia to signs of two algebraic quantities. The two displayed resultant factorizations leave precisely one eligible algebraic zero per quantity; independent rational interval sign certificates prove each occurs once on the physical branch, and no others occur. Sylvester inertia and a positive-definite translation block justify the reduced projective local maximum. Every transition and excluded endpoint is specified. The packaged checker verifies the nonstandard polynomial identities with exact arithmetic; no finite experiments are used as infinite proof.

Klartag (2018) states general covariance/second-variation criteria but does not compute this family. value.rationale: The earlier investigation introduced a natural critical family to understand local variational behavior of the Mahler product but treated its quantitative behavior mainly numerically. This theorem supplies a complete sharp signature classification and rigorous open local-maximum regime, revealing two different algebraic instabilities and giving a precise benchmark for projective stability questions. It is not a chosen isolated parameter, mere numeric verification, or a generic consequence of a preexisting table.
